overview: Italy is one of the most attractive European destinations for Indian students due to its top-ranked public universities, English-taught single-cycle medicine programs, and government-subsidized tuition fees. Students gain deep theoretical grounding and clinical experience across historic teaching hospitals.
universitiesHeading: Top Public Medical Universities in Italy

universities.name: University of Bologna
universities.desc: Founded in 1088, the oldest university in the world, offering an English-taught 6-year Medicine programme.

universities.name: University of Milan
universities.desc: Home to the International Medical School (IMS) with rotations in Milan's premier research hospitals.

universities.name: University of Padua
universities.desc: World-famous for medical discoveries with ancient anatomical theater and cutting-edge labs.

universities.name: University of Pavia
universities.desc: Prestigious Harvey Medicine Course taught entirely in English with high clinical mentorship.

universities.name: Sapienza University of Rome
universities.desc: One of Europe's largest universities with high patient volume across Rome's municipal hospitals.

universities.name: University of Turin
universities.desc: Excellent clinical training in Northern Italy with modern simulation centers and research wards.

faq.question: Is IMAT exam compulsory for MBBS in Italy?
faq.answer: Yes, public universities in Italy require international students to qualify the IMAT (International Medical Admissions Test) conducted annually.

faq.question: What is the fee structure in Italian public universities?
faq.answer: Public university tuition in Italy is subsidized and ranges between €1,000 and €4,000 per year, often reducible based on family income documents.
